set.t: No find reported through 1939 (the 1939 remodel noted no find). The 1939 paper names the old post office the Ruggles store building, so any pipes left would be in its walls and floors. Private downtown building: look only, permission needed. The building appears to survive (2023 imagery): the cream-brick two-storey, third from the Matteson corner.
pinev: Sept 1916 Sanborn sheet 3: "POST OFFICE", two-storey brick, S side of W. Chicago St, 3rd building W of Matteson St, lot 37 (row from the corner: hardware, meat & grocery, P.O., printing).
1910 Sanborn sheet 1: the same lot 37 is labelled "Books" (Ruggles's bookshop), which had become the post office by 1915, matching the sale.
1897 and 1910 Sanborns: the post office was elsewhere, at the E end of the S-side block E of Matteson.

Building appears to survive (Street View, c.2023): a cream/white-brick two-storey with three upper windows and a red awning, third from the corner building; matched by counting from the corner, no datestone seen.
A 1939 remodel article calls it the Ruggles store building, built 1889 and the former post office, which confirms lot 37 is the Ruggles Block and that it stood in 1939.
set.tovw: Lead grade C (treasure thread): three 1915 papers and a 1939 remodel article; never found
